3.4.1.2-r1.burton_quote: disquiets their spirits (as Cyprian saith), torments and terrifies their souls, to make them adore him: and all his study, all his endeavour is to divert them from true Religion, to superstition: and because he is damned himself, and in an error, he would have all the world participate of his errors, and be damned with him
3.4.1.2-r1.translation: They disturb life, trouble sleep, creep even into bodies, break down health, and provoke diseases.

3.4.1.2-r10.burton_quote: ’Tis a wonder, saith Machiavel, Florentinae hist. lib. 1, what slavery King Henry the second endured for the death of Th. Becket, what things he was enjoined by the Pope, and how he submitted himself to do that which in our times a private man would not endure

3.4.1.2-r12.burton_quote: If their Pastors (saith Lavater) had done their duties, and instructed their flocks as they ought, in the Principles of Christian Religion, or had not forbidden them the reading of Scriptures, they had not been as they are

3.4.1.2-r14.burton_quote: The mother of health, key of heaven, a spiritual wing to arear us, the chariot of the holy Ghost, banner of faith, &c.
3.4.1.2-r14.translation: the gate of paradise, the life of angels

3.4.1.2-r15.burton_quote: solitariness, fasting, and that melancholy humour, are the causes of all Hermits’ illusions
3.4.1.2-r15.translation: a mind sick with anxious labours, and then a temperament altered by coarse country food

3.4.1.2-r16.burton_quote: none so subject to visions and dotage in this kind, as such as live solitary lives

3.4.1.2-r17.burton_quote: all your Pythonissas, Sibyls, and pseudoprophets to be mere melancholy

3.4.1.2-r2.burton_quote: A man without religion, is like an horse without a bridle

3.4.1.2-r5.burton_quote: hell with fire and brimstone forever to be tormented

3.4.1.2-r6.burton_quote: he made a delicious Park full of odoriferous flowers and fruits
3.4.1.2-r6.translation: On this side of the water

3.4.1.2-r7.burton_quote: soporiferous potion he so benumbed, that he perceived nothing: and so fast asleep as he was, caused him to be conveyed into this fair garden

3.4.1.2-r8.burton_quote: he cast him into a sleep again, and brought him forth, that when he awaked

3.4.1.2-r9.burton_quote: hath done that without arms, which those Roman Emperors could never achieve with forty legions of soldiers, deposed Kings, and crowned them again with his foot, made friends, and corrected at his pleasure
3.4.1.2-r9.translation: gives laws to the kings of the earth
